proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:rare\text{-}history\text{-}alpha\text{-}only\text{-}obstruction}\), together with Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mixture\text{-}modulus\text{-}length\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\), shows that on the primitive adaptive-design class no finite constant \(C_\alpha\) depending only on \(\alpha\) can satisfy \[\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\le C_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\] uniformly. Indeed, that comparison and the lemma would imply \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star/\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha/C_\alpha>0\), whereas the proposition's admissible sequence has \(p_{\min,n}>0\) in every experiment, \(p_{\min,n}\downarrow0\), and \(\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\to0\). The honest residual question is the following. Fix \(\underline p\in(0,1/2]\) independently of the block counts, block sizes, drift budget, and experiment, and restrict attention to collections of admissible designs satisfying \(p_{bi}(z\mid h)\ge\underline p\) for every \((b,i)\in\mathcal T\), every \(z\in A_b\), and every compatible history \(h\), with the same \(\underline p\) for the whole collection. Does there exist a finite \(C_{\alpha,\underline p}\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and \(\underline p\), such that, uniformly over \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\) and every design in this fixed-floor subclass, \[\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\le C_{\alpha,\underline p}\Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)?\] Equivalently, can the fixed-floor condition be used to construct two priors supported almost surely on \(\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}\) whose assignment-averaged observed-data mixture laws have total variation at most \(\eta_\alpha\) and whose \(\tau_W\)-supports are separated by at least \(C_{\alpha,\underline p}^{-1}\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\), with the sequential likelihood-ratio or deficiency bound derived from the fixed-floor condition rather than by assuming the target separation? This residual question is not a premise of any proved headline result.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current unrestricted question has a negative answer. The established rare-history proposition constructs admissible experiments with \(p_{\min,n}=\alpha/(2n)>0\), \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\), and \(\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\to0\); combined with the established mixture-modulus length lower bound, this rules out the requested comparison with a constant depending only on \(\alpha\). Requiring one fixed \(\underline p>0\) across the compared experiments is an independently interpretable strict subclass of the primitive class and excludes that witness without presupposing the desired target separation.

proposed.justification: The unrestricted comparison is already refuted. This node isolates the strongest directly motivated residual problem suggested by that witness: whether a propensity floor fixed uniformly across the design class is enough to recover a constant-factor comparison, with the constant allowed to depend on that floor.
proposed.gap: The counterexample uses \(p_{\min,n}\downarrow0\), so it does not decide the fixed-floor subclass. Even there, arbitrary outcome-adaptive propensity updates can reweight future histories, and no schedule-supported bounded-total-variation fuzzy-prior construction currently supplies the required sequential mixture-law bound.
proposed.consumer: A positive answer would justify constant-factor minimax calibration only for platform trials that enforce one announced propensity floor uniformly over the compared design family. Until then, the NCC implementation must use the optimized radius only as its proved constructive upper scale.

obligation.what_is_open: For each fixed \(\underline p\in(0,1/2]\), prove or refute the existence of \(C_{\alpha,\underline p}<\infty\) uniformly over the bounded-TV schedules and adaptive designs whose every available-arm propensity is at least the same \(\underline p\).
obligation.obstruction: The shrinking-floor rare-history witness no longer belongs to this subclass, but a fixed pointwise floor alone does not make the assignment tree outcome-oblivious. Fuzzy perturbations must obey the control-total-variation constraint almost surely while their induced outcome histories can still alter every later propensity, so the average score-variance envelope does not itself control the observed-data mixture likelihood ratio.
obligation.attempted: The established overlap-measure argument gives the all-kernel lower bound from any admissible prior pair, and the established rare-history construction refutes the primitive-class comparison. Direct two-point and coordinatewise fuzzy perturbations were also considered, but neither yields a uniform sequential total-variation bound under arbitrary outcome-adaptive propensity updates while retaining almost-sure membership in the bounded-TV schedule class.
obligation.partial_result: For the unrestricted primitive class, the established results give \[\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\] and an admissible sequence for which \[\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M,\qquad \mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\longrightarrow0.\] Hence the original \(\alpha\)-only comparison is false. These generic results remain valid on the fixed-floor subclass, but they do not compare \(\Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\) with \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim narrowing adds the established obstruction as a direct dependency, adds the target and propensity symbols used explicitly by the replacement question, removes the no-longer-load-bearing rare-history stress-test dependency, and synchronizes the node metadata with the fixed-floor residual.

prose_updates.tldr: For the window-weighted finite-population focal-arm effect, the exact cumulative-discrepancy program gives the sharp bounded-drift borrowing bias, and a finite convex program balances that bias against an assignment-law-averaged predictable-AIPW martingale envelope. The projected bias-aware interval is uniformly design-honest and has worst-case expected length at most twice the clipped optimized radius. Every honest observed-data interval kernel also satisfies the generic lower bound \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\), and the masked-focal construction gives a finite-tree computable lower certificate. These bounds do not yield a generic minimax equivalence: the accepted three-block rare-history sequence has a positive floor in every experiment, \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\), and \(\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\to0\) because its floors shrink across the sequence. The only remaining radius-comparison question is explicitly restricted to design families sharing one fixed propensity floor, allows constants to depend on that floor, and is not used by the proved headline. The KKT certificate continues to characterize strict improvement over the concurrent AIPW rule; zero drift gives information-optimal borrowing, while the vacuous-drift all-kernel reduction requires structural invariance of propensity updates to off-window outcomes.

project_justification.gap: Platform-control papers analyze parametric or semiparametric calendar adjustment through bias, type-I error, power, or superpopulation efficiency, while Gaussian convex-class work studies minimax expected length in nonadaptive observation experiments. Neither literature gives a fixed-schedule adaptive-randomization comparison between every honest variable-length interval and a predictable inverse-propensity radius. On the primitive class such an \(\alpha\)-only comparison is not merely missing: the accepted rare-history sequence refutes it even though every member is positive. That witness uses floors tending to zero, leaving open only the independently motivated fixed-floor subclass.
project_justification.niche: The note makes the adaptive assignment tree a first-class design object and keeps the fixed causal schedule distinct from assignment randomness. It combines the exact support function of the bounded-total-variation control-mean class, an implementable predictable-AIPW upper interval, an all-kernel observed-law mixture modulus, a finite-tree masked-focal certificate, and an explicit theorem-level rare-history obstruction. The residual fixed-floor question is separated from this proved spine rather than being used as a hidden premise.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution is the sharp drift-bias dual, the convex-program projected interval with worst-case expected length at most twice its clipped radius, the generic mixture-modulus lower bound for every schedule-independent randomized interval, the computable masked-history lower certificate, and the impossibility of a uniform \(\alpha\)-only radius comparison over the primitive adaptive class. The optimizer certificate compares nonconcurrent-control and concurrent-only AIPW radii, not their all-kernel minimax values. For the NCC package and ACTT-style calibration, the optimized radius is therefore a certified conservative design-based scale; constant-factor minimax calibration is an open research question only after fixing one common propensity floor across the design family. The accepted zero-drift and structurally qualified vacuous-drift boundary results are unchanged.

sampling_model.overlap: The primitive class requires every available arm to have a positive compatible-history propensity within each experiment, but it does not impose one numerical floor uniformly across sequences of experiments. Structural zeros off the availability set are allowed, and information is averaged under each schedule's induced assignment law. The residual converse question separately restricts attention to design families sharing a fixed \(\underline p>0\); that restriction is not part of the proved generic headline.

prose_updates.related_work: LeeWason2020, BofillRoigEtAl2022, and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift compare all-control and concurrent-only platform procedures under linear, step, fixed-effect, mixed-effect, or spline time models, emphasizing bias, type-I error, and power. MarschnerSchou2024 formalizes concurrency through randomized cohorts, and SantacatterinaEtAl2025 studies a superpopulation efficiency problem for the concurrent estimand. Those works motivate the platform setting but do not supply uniform fixed-schedule coverage over a total-variation drift class or minimax expected length over schedule-independent observed-data kernels. LiZhao2026 supplies the predictable-AIPW martingale template; here the scale averages actual inverse-propensity variation under each schedule's adaptive assignment law. ChenLiZhangYe2025, ArmstrongKolesar2018, and CaiLow2004 provide Gaussian bias--variance and mixture-modulus analogies, but their nonadaptive likelihood geometry does not justify comparing that scale with every variable-length interval after outcomes feed back into later assignments. The accepted rare-history construction proves that no constant depending only on \(\alpha\) works on the primitive adaptive class. The generic positive results are instead the observed-law modulus lower bound and the explicit masked-focal certificate. Whether a design family sharing one fixed propensity floor admits a constant depending on \(\alpha\) and that floor remains an isolated residual question, not a claimed literature consequence or headline premise. SawadaNomuraShinozaki2026 selects external-control weights under an estimated bias cap, but its estimand, confounding model, bootstrap interval, and guarantee differ from this fixed-population randomization result. AronowLopatto2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 give bounded finite-population minimax benchmarks without staggered availability, total-variation borrowing, or adaptive-history masking.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The optimized predictable-AIPW radius is a valid constructive upper scale but is not the unrestricted minimax expected-length scale. The counterexample exploits a rare low-propensity branch on which a second-moment interval pays inverse-propensity cost while a variable-length procedure spends part of its permitted miscoverage; every experiment is positive, but its floor decreases with sample size. Fixing one uniform floor across the design family excludes that particular sequence, yet it does not make the assignment rule outcome-oblivious or by itself provide schedule-supported fuzzy priors satisfying the control-total-variation restriction and a sequential likelihood-ratio bound. The existence of a \(C_{\alpha,\underline p}\) comparison on this fixed-floor subclass is therefore left open and is not used downstream. The masked-history expression remains an exact finite-tree computable lower certificate, with no asserted comparison to the optimized radius. The vacuous-drift reduction separately requires propensity invariance across schedules when only off-window outcomes change; predictability alone does not imply that invariance.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target is the window-weighted finite-population focal-arm-versus-control contrast, and assignment is the experiment's only source of randomness. The projected AIPW interval is uniformly honest for every design satisfying the primitive support, boundedness, and drift conditions, without regression consistency or an assumed limit law. The all-kernel mixture-modulus lower bound and finite masked-focal testing certificate are also generic. No universal \(\alpha\)-only equivalence between minimax expected length and the optimized AIPW radius is claimed: an explicit admissible three-block sequence refutes it while maintaining positivity in every experiment. Because that sequence has \(p_{\min,n}\downarrow0\), the sole residual converse question fixes a common \(\underline p>0\) across the compared design family and allows its constant to depend on \(\underline p\); this question is outside the proved headline dependency closure. The KKT result compares nonconcurrent-control and concurrent-only AIPW radii, not the two all-kernel minimax values. At zero drift, equal control block means remove borrowing bias and leave information optimization. At vacuous drift, full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel values agree only under structural invariance of propensity updates to off-window potential-outcome changes holding assignments and window outcomes fixed. The finite three-block linear program retains only its certified zero-drift value \(0.7M\). No claim is made that the drift budget is learned from the trial, that the masked certificate is necessary, that positive-drift finite-LP values are known, or that a fixed propensity floor already proves the residual converse.
